title: Applications
summary: What ecosystem dapps are, how they expose tools to your agent, and how their flow travels with an x402 toll.

blocks.text: An application (dapp) extends what your agent can do: each one exposes a set of tools the agent calls while reasoning. A dapp's entire flow travels the x402 gateway: every use pays its micro-toll with your account's dPaaS wallet.

sections.heading: Adding an application to your account

items: Open Services in the navbar: you'll see the catalog with its resource and status.
Press Add to account on the dapp you want: the api records the link with a snapshot (network, payer, date).
From that moment, the agent receives its tools automatically on the next turn.
Verify in the dashboard (Tools by apps) that its tools show up marked as on your account.

blocks.title: Nothing installs on the device
blocks.text: Adding an app installs nothing on the ESP32: tools live on the server and the device only renders results.

On every turn, brain builds the tool list = core (status, Solana, x402) + tools from YOUR added dapps. The model decides which to call and with what arguments; the api executes each call against the real dapp, passing through the toll.
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/agent/tools | jq '[.[] | .app // "core"] | group_by(.) | map({app: .[0], tools: length})'

Every protected resource answers 402 with an invoice when it carries no valid payment. Your account's dPaaS wallet signs the settlement (you never sign by hand) and the invoice is consumed once: replaying it returns 409.
